narrative_markdown:
## Today's Forecast

Morning showers and thunderstorms will bring 9.1 mm of rain with onset between 10:00 and 15:00, reaching a high of 29°C / 85°F and an overnight low of 19°C / 65°F. Thunder possible from the morning, peaking this evening. Skies will be mostly cloudy early, becoming partly cloudy by midday, and returning to mostly cloudy into the evening and overnight. Wind will be east-northeasterly overnight, turning southwest by midday, with peak gusts reaching 39 km/h (21 kt). The peak UV index reaches 9.4. Air quality is AQI 79 at Kisumu Airport, the highest of three reporting stations. As of 06:01, reports through 03:00: rain from 01:00; no thunder; high so far 19°C / 66°F; low so far 19°C / 66°F; peak sustained 9 km/h; sky mostly cloudy.

## Extended Outlook

Warming through Wednesday, with showers and thunderstorms likely each day. Skies mostly cloudy Monday, then partly cloudy Tuesday and Wednesday. Wednesday's call: rain, 100%, with all four models wet; highs around 31 °C. Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) calls it wet. At this lead ICON has the best record, right 77% of the time over 64 checks.

Further out, temperatures and winds much the same through Sunday, with rain and thunderstorms likely Thursday and Friday, and showers and thunderstorms possible Saturday and Sunday. Thursday: all four models wet, highs 28 to 31 °C. Friday: all four models wet, the week's wettest day at 22 mm on average, highs 28 to 30 °C. Saturday: all three models that reach it wet, highs around 28 °C, thunder possible rather than likely.

Only GFS, ECMWF and ICON reach past Friday. GFS is the wetter solution from Thursday to Friday; ECMWF, ICON and UKMO keep it drier. Sunday's call: rain, 100%, with both models wet; highs around 30 °C. At this lead ECMWF has the best record, right 77% of the time over 60 checks.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential

Convective instability today: UKMO 4420 J/kg, ECMWF 2280 J/kg, GFS 1240 J/kg and ICON 1120 J/kg. Thunder likely; any thunderstorm brings sudden gusts well above the 39 km/h (21 kt) forecast.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters

Peak gust 28 km/h (15 kt). Any thunderstorm brings sudden gusts well above this figure; the water is unsafe while one is nearby.

## Detailed Discussion

### Synoptic Overview

Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the northwest (1010 hPa) and highest toward the southeast (1016 hPa) — a 6 hPa spread, a moderate large-scale gradient. Pressure is also falling toward the north, south, southeast — a large-scale feature building in that direction, though this sampling cannot say how fast or whether it will reach here. Pressure overhead is near-steady. Sampling is a nine-point ring at 12-degree spacing, so this locates a direction, not a centre or a front. Across the basin's 5 points, pressure today sits between 1014.5 and 1016.2 hPa, near-steady over three days (-1.3 hPa). Pressure here over the last 24 hours: -1.3 hPa.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes

On rain the record ranks ICON first at Day+3, right 77% of the last 30 checks and ECMWF first at Day+7, right 77% of the last 30 checks. On today's high UKMO is the warmest model at 28.7 °C and ECMWF the coolest at 28.1 °C; the call's 29.3 °C sits at the warm end. Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) calls a high of 30.0 °C and rain, agreeing with the call on rain. At Day+0, no model is meaningfully better than the others here yet. At Day+7, ECMWF is the strongest rain caller here and GFS the weakest. At Day+0, Best Match slightly under-forecasts peak wind here.
